requirement: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page, and each rendered requirement and example MUST be followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and, when an index exists, to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale:
I found no gaps. I judged from the cited source items only and did not read other files. **Obligations and the code that carries them out** 1. **Definition badge links to the detail page.** `replace_definitions` (src/lib.rs) computes `detail_href` with `chapter_href` and `plan.detail_path`. It renders the badge as an `` when a detail page exists, and as a `` otherwise. This covers requirements and examples, and it excludes terms, which the text does not cover. 2. **"See evidence" link after each rendered requirement and example.** `replace_definitions` appends `

See evidence

` after the body whenever `detail_href` is set. 3. **Detail page links back to the anchored definition badge.** `render_detail_page` (src/index.rs) emits `[View definition](chapter_href(detail_path, definition.path, Some(kind.anchor(name))))`. `DefinitionKind::anchor` (src/lib.rs) builds the `habeas-req-` anchor, which matches the `id` set on the badge. 4. **Detail page links to the index when one exists.** `render_detail_page` adds `[Requirements index](…)` only when `index_path` is `Some`. `DetailPlan::populate` passes `self.index_path` to it, and also links the index rows to the detail pages. 5. **Reference badges keep linking to the definition.** `reference_badge`, called from `replace_inline_references`, builds an `` to the target definition's path and anchor. 6. **Links resolve when a name contains `.md`.** `chapter_href` rewrites `.md` to `%2Emd` in the whole href, including the anchor. **Tests** - `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index` (src/lib.rs) checks the badge `href` and the "See evidence" link for a requirement, an example, and `cli.mdbook`. It also checks the "View definition" link, including the `%2Emd` form, and that no index link appears when there is no index. - `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` (src/index.rs) checks the badge `href` when an index exists. It also checks the "Requirements index" and "View definition" links on the detail page, and the index-row links to the detail pages. - `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` (src/lib.rs) checks `chapter_href` for names containing `.md`, in both directions and with the anchor. - `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` (src/lib.rs) checks that impl, cite, and test badges link to the definition. All four tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. `is_detail_path` is a trivial predicate with no obligation of its own, so it needs no separate test.
